title: Support a straightedge at its Bessel points
instruction: Support the 30 cm straightedge at its Bessel points: stand the two support blocks on the surface plate, lay the straightedge across them, level, with each support 22 percent of its length in from its end, and let go of it.
context: Gauge bars and precision straightedges are supported at their Bessel points, 0.2203 of the length (22 %) in from each end, where sagging changes the length of the bar's neutral axis least; the Airy points (0.2113) keep its end faces parallel, and overall sag is least at about 0.2232. This straightedge is deliberately unmarked, so the points have to be found by measuring, while handling a long part with both hands.
setup: The table top (oak) is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two arms 61 cm apart on a table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward and y to the left, in cm. A black granite surface plate (16 x 40 x 2 cm tall, its 40 cm along y; a thin stand-in for a real plate, which is much thicker) is fixed at (29, 0). An aluminium straightedge, an unmarked bar 2.5 x 30 x 2.5 cm (its 30 cm along y, 0.5 kg), lies on a red felt cloth (6 x 34 x 0.3 cm, its 34 cm along y) on the table at (15, 0). Two blue-painted steel support blocks (3 x 3 x 4 cm tall, 0.25 kg each) stand on the table at (18, 24) and (18, -24).
scoring: The straightedge counts as supported when both blocks stand upright (within 5 degrees) on the surface plate and the straightedge rests across them, released: still, both grippers more than 3 cm from it, its length level within 2 degrees and along y within 5 degrees (either way round), a face flat on the blocks within 5 degrees, one block on either side of its middle and each under it, and its underside within 1.5 mm of each block's top. Its Bessel points are 6.6 cm (6.61) in from each end, 16.8 cm (16.78) apart. Score: 0 unless supported; 0.5 supported; plus 0.25 for each block whose centre is within 1 cm of a Bessel point, measured along the straightedge (one block per point). The 1 cm also takes in the Airy points (6.34 cm in) and the least-sag points (6.70 cm in). So leaving everything as it starts, a block knocked over or off the plate, the straightedge on the plate, or the straightedge still held all score 0. On real arms, measure each block's centre from the straightedge's nearer end with a tape measure (read to 2 mm) and check level with a spirit level; judge by eye from a photo of the end state that the blocks stand upright, the straightedge sits on both along y, and the grippers are clear of it. The 1.5 mm, 5 degree and 3 cm limits are checked in simulation only.
reset_notes: Lay the straightedge back on its cloth and stand the support blocks back at their positions.
fidelity: Approximate. The straightedge is a rigid bar that cannot sag, so where it is supported is scored from the geometry, not from a measured deflection. The support blocks stand in for adjustable supports, and the 2 cm granite plate for a real, much thicker one. The simulator gives loose objects rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Letting go is checked from each gripper's fingertip centre, which the task's embodiment adds to what the scorer sees.
